STATUS: fail

SUMMARY: The redeem logic meets every listed criterion and hostile input, and the mutation checks show the tests catch `>=`, `or`-defaulting, no-mark, and check-order mutations. The one real defect is a check-then-set race on the `used` flag: one token can be redeemed by several threads at once. The diff has no concurrent test, so nothing catches it.

FILES TOUCHED: none (probes ran in /tmp/tmp.Uhwvk8rDWu; repo git status unchanged)

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Race on single-use: `redeem_reset_token` reads `record["used"]`, then sets it, with no lock. Widened copy (sleep 0.01 between check and write), 8 threads on one token, 200 rounds: `rounds with !=1 success: 200 of 200`, first round `successes 8 errs []`. Unwidened, the window is too narrow to hit (0 of 200). Fix: a `threading.Lock` held across the used-check and the mark. The diff also needs its own concurrent test, which it lacks.
- [minor] NaN is not rejected. `redeem_reset_token(t, now=float('nan'))` returns the username even when the token was issued at 1000, and a NaN `issued_at` never expires. Not in the criteria; not reproduced as a criterion failure.
- [minor] The removed `test_unknown_token` was replaced rather than kept. The new test covers the same case, so this is a style note only.

CHECKS:
- `python3 -m unittest discover` on a copy of the repo -> pass (19 tests)
- Criteria probe (now=0 issue, 1800/1801 redeem, float 1000.0/2800.0 vs 2800.5, redeem before issue, exact `InvalidToken` type for "" and unknown) -> pass
- Mutation `> RESET_TTL` → `>= RESET_TTL` -> caught (2 errors)
- Mutation `if now is None` → `if not now` at redeem -> caught (2 errors)
- Same mutation at issue -> caught (1 failure)
- Mutation: drop `record["used"] = True` -> caught (7 failures, 1 error)
- Mutation: check expiry before used -> caught (1 error)
- Concurrency, 8 threads × 200 rounds, unwidened -> pass (0 bad rounds; not sufficient on its own)
- Concurrency, widened copy with sleep between check and write -> FAIL (200 of 200 rounds gave 8 successes)
- Seeded property test, 5000 cases with a reference model (boundary values, floats, skew, double redeem) -> pass, no failing input
- README line "30 minutes and single use" matches the behaviour -> pass
- Project checklist: patterns match (module-local exception subclasses, tests in tests/test_auth.py, README line) -> pass

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should the orchestrator require the lock fix plus a concurrent test before this ships? The race only shows when the check and write are separated by a delay. Under the current code the window is tiny, but the criterion "single use" is not enforced under concurrency.
